Formal mixture analysis via quantile g-computation

Source: R/qgcomp-mixture.R
run_mixture_qgcomp.Rd

Wraps qgcomp::qgcomp.noboot() or qgcomp::qgcomp.boot() on pseudobulk data for cell-type-specific exposure mixture analysis. Unlike run_sc_mixture (simplified screening), it reports a confidence interval and p-value for the overall mixture effect and, without bootstrapping, the positive and negative exposure weights estimated by qgcomp.

Usage

run_mixture_qgcomp(
  x,
  exposures,
  celltype,
  celltype_col = "cell_type",
  target_genes = NULL,
  covariates = NULL,
  q = 4L,
  bootstrap = FALSE,
  B = 200L,
  min_cells = 10L
)

Arguments

x

A SingleCellExposomeExperiment. Each cell's donor is read from the colData column named by sampleColumn(x).

exposures

Character vector. Exposure variable names, distinct. Each name must be a syntactic R name (see make.names) because it goes into the model formula, and cannot be ., ... or a name such as ..1, which R reads specially there. The names y, weights and id__ cannot be used: the response is called y, and qgcomp adds columns called weights and id__ to the model data. With bootstrap = FALSE a name cannot contain _q either, which qgcomp removes from the names of the weights it returns.

celltype

Character. Target cell type.

celltype_col

Character. colData column with cell type labels. Default "cell_type".

target_genes

Character vector (optional). Genes to summarise. Default: top 20 most variable.

covariates

Character vector (optional). Columns of exposureData; an unknown name is an error, and so is an exposure listed here. Names must be syntactic and cannot be y, weights, id__, ., ... or a name such as ..1, as for exposures.

q

Integer. Number of quantile bins. Default 4.

bootstrap

Logical. If TRUE, use qgcomp.boot() for bootstrap confidence intervals. Default FALSE (faster; a t interval on the residual degrees of freedom, see Details).

B

Integer. Number of bootstrap replicates (only if bootstrap = TRUE). Default 200.

min_cells

Integer. Default 10.

Value

A one-row DataFrame with columns celltype, mixture_effect (the overall mixture effect \(\psi\)), mixture_se, ci_lower and ci_upper (95% confidence interval for \(\psi\)), mixture_pvalue (for the interval and the p-value see Details), n_donors, n_genes and method ("qgcomp.noboot" or "qgcomp.boot"). metadata(result) holds:

positive_weights

Named numeric. Exposures that increase the response, with relative weights; NULL when bootstrap = TRUE, because qgcomp.boot() does not estimate weights.

negative_weights

Named numeric. Exposures that decrease the response; NULL when bootstrap = TRUE.

target_genes

The genes whose mean log-CPM is the response.

fit

The qgcomp model object (for plotting and further analysis).

Details

Quantile g-computation (Keil et al. 2020) estimates the overall effect of jointly increasing all exposures by one quantile, and without bootstrapping decomposes it into positive and negative contributions. The weights are interpretable only when the exposure effects are of a similar shape (Keil et al. 2020).

The pseudobulk response is the mean log-CPM of the target genes over donors with complete exposure and covariate data.

Without bootstrapping, mixture_pvalue is a two-sided t test of \(\psi\) on the residual degrees of freedom of the fitted model, and ci_lower and ci_upper are the matching t interval. qgcomp.noboot() itself uses the null degrees of freedom minus the number of exposures for its p-value, which leaves the covariates out, and a normal interval; its own values are kept in metadata(result)$fit. With bootstrap = TRUE the p-value and the interval are those of qgcomp.boot(); the call stops when qgcomp.boot() returns no p-value for \(\psi\).

Comparison with run_sc_mixture:

Featurerun_sc_mixturerun_mixture_qgcomp
CI for overall effectNoYes (t interval or bootstrap)
Pos/neg weightsNoYes (without bootstrap)
P-value for overall effectNoYes
SpeedFastModerate
Minimum n510+ recommended

References

Keil AP et al. (2020). A quantile-based g-computation approach to addressing the effects of exposure mixtures. Environ Health Perspect 128:047004. doi:10.1289/EHP5838

Examples

# Requires the qgcomp package
library(SingleCellExperiment); library(S4Vectors)
set.seed(1)
counts <- matrix(rpois(5000, 8), nrow = 50,
    dimnames = list(paste0("G", 1:50), paste0("c", 1:100)))
sce <- SingleCellExperiment(assays = list(counts = counts),
    colData = DataFrame(cell_id = paste0("c", 1:100),
        donor_id = rep(paste0("D", 1:10), each = 10),
        cell_type = rep(c("Mono", "NK"), 50)))
exp_mat <- matrix(rnorm(30), nrow = 10,
    dimnames = list(paste0("D", 1:10), c("E1", "E2", "E3")))
scee <- build_scee(sce, exp_mat, sample_col = "donor_id")
if (requireNamespace("qgcomp", quietly = TRUE)) {
    mix <- run_mixture_qgcomp(scee,
        exposures = c("E1", "E2", "E3"),
        celltype = "Mono", celltype_col = "cell_type",
        min_cells = 3L)
    mix
    metadata(mix)$positive_weights
    metadata(mix)$negative_weights
}
#> E1 
#>  1
